Collaboration & Delivery

**JOB DESCRIPTION – Principal Product Solution Engineer**
**About Intelex**
At Intelex, we’re not just building software; we’re empowering organizations worldwide to create safer, more sustainable, and higher-performing workplaces. As a global leader in Environment, Health, Safety (EHS), Quality, and Sustainability Management Software, Intelex is dedicated to transforming the way companies manage workplace safety, compliance, and operational excellence. Our technology enables companies to proactively manage risk to keep people and the planet safe.
**About the role**
The Product Solution Engineering Team sits at the intersection of customer pain and product strategy. We've evolved from traditional scrum teams to cross-functional squads building features that solve real customer problems at scale. We also partner with our ecosystem to extend capabilities beyond our core platform, ensuring a cohesive experience for customers.
As a **Principal Product Solution Engineer,**you'll build scalable configuration solutions using low-code platforms (primarily the Intelex platform) and experiment with AI-assisted development to validate product hypotheses faster. You'll work embedded in product squads, translating customer requirements into technical solutions that influence our roadmap. For this senior role, you'll also bring deep platform expertise to guide build-versus-partner decisions and ensure our partner ecosystem aligns with product strategy.
**How you’ll make a difference:**
**Solution Validation & Building (50%)**
* Design and build advanced configuration solutions on the Intelex platform for complex customer use cases
* Progress solutions through Build 1 (5 customers) → Build 2 (50 customers) → Build 3 (500+ customers) maturity stages
* Identify patterns across customer requirements to build generalizable solutions rather than one-offs
* Partner with Engineering teams from day one to ensure smooth productization handoff
* Translate customer pain points into technical requirements for product squads
* Participate in Voice of Customer (VOC) sessions and occasional customer site visits
**Platform & Partner Strategy (30%)**
* Contribute to "build versus partner" decisions for applications and integrations, leveraging your deep understanding of Intelex platform capabilities and partner ecosystem
* Review design of partner-developed applications to ensure platform integrity, scalability, and alignment with product strategy
* Provide technical guidance on partner integration feasibility and architecture
* Educate internal teams (Services, Support, Sales) on Intelex platform capabilities and partner offerings
* Collaborate with Partnership Org to establish partner development guidelines
**Innovation & Team Leadership (20%)**
* Experiment with AI-assisted development tools (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) to build rapid prototypes for validation
* Mentor PSE team members on Intelex platform best practices, scalable configuration patterns, and common pitfalls
* Contribute to our evolving Rapid Validation Playbook based on what works in practice
* Share insights that inform partner development frameworks and integration standards
**What you bring to the table:**
**Required Experience & Skills**
* 4-6 years building solutions on low-code/no-code platforms (e.g., Salesforce, ServiceNow, OutSystems, Mendix, PowerApps, Intelex)
* 2+ years Intelex platform experience strongly preferred - we need deep platform expertise to guide partner decisions and mentor the team
* Proven ability to scale solutions from prototype to production—you've seen what happens when one-off solutions need to serve hundreds of customers
* Strong systems thinking: you naturally identify patterns across use cases and design for generalization, not just the immediate request
* Experience working in product-focused environments where iteration speed matters more than architectural purity
* Partner ecosystem familiarity: you've implemented partner integrations or applications and understand how they extend platform capabilities
* Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change—our processes are defined but evolving, and you'll help shape them
**Preferred Skills**
* Understanding of low-code platforms beyond Intelex (Salesforce, ServiceNow, etc.) - helpful for bringing external best practices
* EHSQ domain knowledge (understanding of compliance, auditing, incident management, etc.)
* Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools (GitHub Copilot, Goose, Cursor, Claude Code, Replit, Lovable, etc.)
* Basic understanding of web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) for customization work
* Experience with remote collaboration across time zones
**Work Traits We Value**
* Pragmatic builder: You'd rather ship a working solution today than a perfectly architected solution next quarter
* Customer-obsessed: You care deeply about solving real problems, not just checking technical boxes
* Intellectually curious: You experiment with new tools and approaches, then share what you learn
* Collaborative: You work well embedded in product squads and don't need to be the hero
* Resilient: You're comfortable being uncomfortable – rapid iteration means things change, and that excites rather than drains you
**Education**
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related technical field. Equivalent practical experience building platform-based solutions will also be considered.
**Who This Role Is NOT For**
Be honest with yourself before applying. This role isn't a fit if you:
* Want to write production code in Java/Python/C# all day (that's Engineering's role)
* Need highly structured processes and clear 12-month roadmaps (we're iterating rapidly)
* Prefer deep technical architecture over pragmatic solutions (we optimize for speed of learning)
* View this as pure partner management (you'll contribute to partner strategy, but 70% of your time is building and validating product solutions)
*We value thoughtful, specific answers over generic cover letters. Show us how you think, not just what you've done.*

Our diverse Product & Engineering team values innovation, collaboration, and the continuous improvement of our platform. We offer a dynamic work environment where employees can grow and thrive while working on cutting-edge technology that shapes the future of AI and search.
At AlphaSense, we believe that diverse experiences and perspectives are critical to our success. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves.
### About the Role
AlphaSense is moving beyond search with SuperAnalyst: AI-powered workflows that monitor change, update outputs, and surface what matters as situations evolve. Mobile brings that intelligence into the moments when customers are away from their desks.
Delivering those experiences through native applications presents a distinctive engineering challenge: services evolve continuously while released apps remain in customers' hands. Designing for that reality creates an opportunity to shape how AlphaSense builds shared product capabilities, with benefits reaching well beyond iOS and Android.
Based in Mobile Engineering, you will use a close connection to customer and product needs to shape backend systems across engineering organizations. You will help decide which cross-team problems to tackle and where architectural investment will have the greatest impact, then work with the owning engineers to build and prove the solution in production.

* **Shape the systems behind product experiences:** Set technical direction for client-facing APIs and the backend architecture behind them. Work with service and platform owners to simplify how backend services connect and support product workflows across clients.
* **Lead across engineering organizations:** Work across application, search and AI, and shared platform teams to shape technical priorities around customer and product needs. * **Turn architecture into production systems:** Lead delivery of services and subsystems that span team boundaries, from choosing the technical approach to implementing the hardest parts and proving them in production. Design these systems for reuse beyond the initial use case.
* **Shape shared identity and access:** Partner with User Management and platform teams to evolve how users authenticate, maintain sessions, and access product capabilities across Web and Mobile. Build native-client requirements into shared identity and configuration services.
* **Leave engineers and teams stronger:** Help engineers deepen their technical judgment and build the expertise to own and evolve the systems you deliver together. Combine hands-on delivery with coaching and reusable patterns, whether embedding with an existing team or bringing engineers together around a focused mission with leadership support.
### What We're Looking For
Your strongest experience should be in backend and platform engineering, with client needs informing your architectural decisions. Prior iOS or Android development experience is not required.
### Required:
* Deep production backend and distributed-systems expertise, including service boundaries, data ownership, consistency, failure recovery, and integration models. A track record of simplifying complex architectures with impact across teams or domains.
* Strong hands-on engineering experience, with significant personal contributions to production code and system evolution. Ability to develop a deep understanding of unfamiliar codebases and turn investigation into sound engineering decisions.
* Experience designing client-facing REST and GraphQL APIs, with sound judgment about business-logic placement, product states, and backward compatibility. Understanding of how mobile lifecycle and network constraints affect backend design.
* Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, entitlements, and session management, including trust boundaries and the security implications of client-service interactions.
* Experience improving customer-visible reliability and performance across client and backend systems, with practical expertise in observability and production validation.
* A track record of leading consequential technical change across teams through influence rather than reporting authority.
* Product and stakeholder leadership that connects technical decisions to customer value. Demonstrated success challenging assumptions and building alignment with senior leaders, balancing immediate customer and product needs with durable foundations other teams can build on.
### Preferred:
* Experience building production systems for AI-powered search, research, or analysis workflows.

* Experience designing shared configuration or service discovery for multi-tenant platforms and dedicated customer environments.

Georgia, Poland, Portugal, NigeriaRelease Engineer
Share
We are looking for a senior engineer to take technical ownership of the release process for two large open-source infrastructure products, maintained on behalf of a US enterprise software vendor. This is deliberately not a feature-building role: the work is vulnerability remediation, dependency and runtime upgrades, keeping builds passing across all supported platforms, and shipping a small number of thoroughly validated releases each year.
You will act as the technical owner of the release train and as the client's primary engineering contact, which means the position combines deep hands-on work in Go and Erlang/OTP with direct, English-language communication with the customer's package, product, and documentation teams. You will also guide and review a mid-level engineer working alongside you, sharing knowledge so that no critical area of the codebase depends on one person.

* 5+ years in backend, platform, or release engineering
* Production Go experience in a large, multi-service codebase, modules, dependency management, testing
* Genuine hands-on Erlang/OTP: reading, patching, compiling, and releasing services; comfortable with rebar3 and dependencies pinned to forked repos and branches which is the most demanding part of the role, passing familiarity isn't enough
* Practical vulnerability-management experience: reading advisories and scanner output (OSV, Dependabot, Snyk, or similar), reasoning about transitive risk, and choosing between patching, upgrading, and replacing a component
* Demonstrated ownership of releases for a shipped product: version strategy, channel promotion, changelogs, go/no-go decisions
* Solid Linux fundamentals, shell scripting, Docker
* Persistence to unpick long, uninformative build failures
* Experience mentoring and reviewing other engineers' work
* English at C1, written and spoken, for direct client communication
* Comfort working autonomously with low supervision — quiet stretches, then intense release periods
* Experience using AI coding assistants (Cursor, Copilot, or similar) day to day
## Would be a plus
* Experience in a large configuration-management or infrastructure-automation ecosystem, packaging toolchains, release automation, verification suites
* Ruby and Bundler; hosted CI/CD platforms and pipeline maintenance
* OpenResty/Lua, PostgreSQL, OpenSearch or Elasticsearch, Nginx
* Experience supporting products in maintenance mode or nearing end-of-life
* Experience assembling air-gapped release bundles for enterprise customers
* Awareness of FIPS-validated cryptography constraints on upgrades; declarative database migration tooling
* Experience building AI-powered solutions or integrating AI pipelines/APIs
## You Are Going To
* Own the release train end to end for both products: dependency bumps, build, test, package, promotion from unstable to stable, and technical release notes
* Triage vulnerability reports, judge exploitability and severity, and choose the remediation route, patch, upgrade, replace, or defer within agreed limits on certified cryptography, OS compatibility, and offline distribution bundles

Exciting opportunity for an experienced Product Manager, or an aspiring Product Owner ready for the next step, to join a fast-paced high growth PE backed global software provider and help shape the direction of our investigation software within the Product team.
Our Altia
By being a trusted technology partner, we empower the government, public and private sector with actionable intelligence solutions to combat increasingly complex crimes. Specialising in crime reduction, we help make the world a safer place.
Initially based in the UK, Altia has grown significantly in recent years through expansion of international operations. We currently have a team of around 90 employees, supporting a wide variety of clients globally.
Our clients include law enforcement agencies, government departments and agencies, regulatory & tax authorities, and private sector customers – who all trust and rely on our investigation software to help them deliver targeted results. Our solutions significantly save time on investigations and reduce costs in areas such as criminal and civil investigations, fraud and financial investigation, incident and investigation management and a variety of covert fields.
Our experienced team is dedicated to providing our clients with the support and care they need, ensuring they are able to get the most from our ever-evolving specialist investigation software solutions.
The role of Product Manager will be based at our Nottingham office and you will be reporting to the Director of Product. Whilst we operate a hybrid working policy, you will be expected to attend the office on a regular basis following completion of your induction and training.
This is a product role with an unusual design constraint: what we build gets tested in court. Our customers’ work is picked apart by defence teams and inspectorates, which means ours has to stand up too. It is demanding, and it is the best design constraint we know — it makes the thinking sharper, the evidence better, and the product more defensible.
We are looking for a career product person: genuinely close to customers, with the commercial instinct to tell what matters now from what matters next, and the judgement to decide which problem to solve first.
Our business is still growing and now is an exciting time to join our friendly and self-motivated team! At Altia we have a common mission and vision that underpins all that we do. We act with honesty, integrity, and mutual respect towards our customers and one another, working as one team. Our commitment to this is showcased through our achievement of the globally recognised Great Place to Work certification for the second year running. We embrace challenge in order to ensure the most innovative and relevant solutions are developed, always with the end customer in mind.
Please note that the successful candidate will be required to be security vetted. For this reason, you must have been in UK residence for 3 continuous years prior to employment and provide proof of address for the previous 5 years. If you do not fit this criteria and also know that there may be anything hindering you from being vetted successfully, then you will not pass initial screening as security vetting is required by every Altia employee.
The Role
Drafting documentation has never been faster. It still has to be done, done well, and done differently, now that agentic AI sits inside the delivery lifecycle. What has not become easier is the judgement underneath it — knowing which customer problem matters most, what to build first, and what will still matter in three years. That judgement is what this role is for.
You will have exposure across the whole Altia portfolio — case and intelligence management, financial investigation, open-source intelligence, and critical incident management — working closely with the Product Managers and Product Owners already here. Your focus will settle on a defined area of that portfolio, designing capabilities and AI skills around how investigators actually work, finding the differentiators, validating them with the market, and building on the agentic AI work already well underway.
Our customers are law enforcement agencies, regulators, government departments and financial crime teams in the UK and internationally. Because their work is scrutinised, ours has to be defensible. Our approach is human-led and AI-accelerated: everything we build must be capable of being explained, evidenced and stood behind.
This is a dual-horizon role. You will keep the depth needed to make good product decisions alongside delivery teams, while lifting your focus toward market differentiation, customer discovery and commercial impact. You will report to the Director of Product and operate with a high degree of autonomy.
Key Responsibilities:
* Customer discovery and insight. Lead structured discovery — interviews, research, workshops and customer advisory groups — and stay genuinely close to the people who use our software. Define user segments, personas and end-to-end journeys, and identify the moments that matter most.
* Product strategy and roadmap. Shape the long-term vision for your products alongside the Director of Product, own the near-term roadmap, and make and defend prioritisation decisions that balance customer value, commercial impact and delivery feasibility.
* Market intelligence and differentiation. Maintain a current, actionable view of the competitive landscape. Identify whitespace, emerging trends and threats, and translate them into strategic recommendations. Articulate why our products win now and why they will still win in three years.
* Commercial impact. Treat commercial outcomes as a first-class product concern. Understand the levers — upsell potential, churn risk, licence utilisation — and make sure product decisions contribute to revenue growth, retention and expansion of ARR.
* Agentic AI in the product and in the process. Design AI capabilities and skills around real investigative workflows, holding the line on transparency and defensibility. Help evolve our product artefacts and ways of working now that agentic AI sits inside the development lifecycle.
* Go-to-market and positioning. Partner with Sales, Marketing and Altia Solutions on value propositions, positioning, launches, tenders and competitive responses, and contribute to pricing and packaging decisions informed by market and customer insight.
* Product planning and feature design. Lead requirements definition, produce clear and well-scoped user stories with robust acceptance criteria, define MVPs and release candidates, and resolve scope questions quickly during delivery.
* Delivery team collaboration. Keep delivery teams supplied with a well-prepared, clearly prioritised backlog and agreed sprint goals, validate what is built against what was specified, and act as the point of escalation for product decisions during a sprint.
* Product expertise and enablement. Act as an internal authority on your products, resolve complex questions from Sales, Support and customers, and work with Support to turn recurring issues into strategic solutions rather than tactical workarounds.
What you can bring to the role:
* A career in product management, with evidence of owning a roadmap and influencing strategic decisions — or experience as a Product Owner or Business Analyst who is ready for the step up.
* Genuine closeness to customers. You seek them out, run your own research, and form your own view rather than relying on second-hand accounts.
* Commercial instinct — a feel for what impacts revenue now and what positions the product for what comes next.
* Judgement under ambiguity. The ability to decide which problem matters most and what to build first, and to explain and defend those decisions to customers, colleagues and the board.
* The confidence to ask the awkward questions early — of customers, of colleagues, and of your own assumptions.
* Comfort working with agentic AI as part of both the product and the process, with a clear-eyed view of where it helps, where it needs a human in the loop, and where it must never be relied on unsupervised.
* The ability to synthesise market data, customer insight and usage analytics into clear, evidence-based strategic narratives.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, able to influence across commercial, technical and operational teams.
* Experience working in or alongside agile delivery teams, with a clear understanding of backlog management and requirements definition.
* An interest in — or experience of — regulated, evidential or investigative environments where what you build has to withstand external scrutiny; for example policing, law enforcement, regulatory bodies, financial crime, insolvency, defence or national security. Desirable rather than essential: we will teach the domain to the right product person.

# QA Engineer - Slots, Crypto & Live Casino
## **About us**
Arena Entertainment is a digital entertainment company building online platforms and games since 2021, with brands including MetaWin, WOW Vegas, Hit.com, BetZoo Media and Rolla. We run an AI-first engineering culture: we expect the tools to change every few months, and we hire people who are energised by that rather than tired of it.
## **About the role**
We build and operate casino games across MetaWin, HIT and our social casino platforms. The role covers three product lines, and you'll work across all of them:
* Slots - our own titles such as Legend of Tartarus, Candy Cash and Rise of Cetus: paytables, bonus rounds, free spins, multiplier ladders and RTP-relevant behaviour.
* Crypto originals - Plinko, Roulette, Crash and Prime Dice: on-chain settlement, token precision and provably-fair verification.
* Live casino - streamed dealer tables: real-time game state, bet windows, stream quality and third-party provider integrations.
These are real-money products. When a payout is wrong, it's wrong in someone's wallet so the bar for correctness is higher than most web QA roles, and the interesting problems live below the UI: settlement maths, wallet reconciliation, provably-fair verification, real-time socket traffic, and the network layer where the truth actually lives.
You'll join a small games QA function in a senior seat, working alongside our existing QA lead who brings deep domain knowledge of our games, our platform and where the bodies are buried. Senior here means you set the standard: you own test strategy for the titles you take, you decide what gets automated and how, and you're the person the team believes when you say something is or isn't ready to ship.
The work is a genuine mix of manual and automated testing, and it stays that way. New builds need someone playing them properly exploratory work is how most of the interesting bugs surface, and live tables in particular have to be sat at and played. Alongside that, we run a Playwright/TypeScript harness with page objects, payout specs and network-intercept probes, with AI-assisted authoring using Claude, and we're actively pushing into agent-driven testing: agents that explore a build, generate and maintain specs, triage failures and cut the regression cost of shipping several titles in parallel.
Coverage is still expanding and the AI side is still being invented. You'll have real influence over both, rather than inheriting someone else's finished framework.
The roadmap runs several titles in parallel. If you like variety, ownership, and finding the bug nobody else would have caught, this is a good fit.
## **What you'll do**
### **Slot testing**
* Design and execute test plans for new slot releases, from first playable build through to live production.
* Verify win evaluation against the maths spec: symbol combinations, line and ways evaluation, scatter counts, wild substitution checked against the API round response, not the number the reels animate to.
* Test bonus and free-spin features end to end: trigger and retrigger conditions, spin counts carrying over, sticky and expanding wilds, feature-buy where offered, and what the feature pays versus what it should.
* Exercise multiplier ladders, cascading and tumble wins, progressive and jackpot contributions, and win-cap truncation at the max-win boundary.
* Cover bet handling in full: bet levels and coin denominations, min and max stake per currency, autoplay with loss limits and single-win stops, turbo and quick spin, and rapid repeated spins.
* Reconcile the wallet on every round balance before and after, insufficient funds mid-autoplay, currency and denomination switching mid-session.
* Break the states nobody demos: refresh mid-spin, disconnect mid-bonus, browser back, session resume, network loss during free spins, and a round settled twice.
* Validate game history and round replay against what actually happened, including round IDs traceable to the transaction record.
* Run long or seeded sessions to sanity-check outcome distribution against expected RTP and volatility, and flag anything that drifts.
* Check paytable text against actual behaviour, plus max-win and promotional wording, currency formatting and locale variants.
### **Crypto game testing**
* Test our crypto originals Plinko, Roulette, Crash, Prime Dice where settlement is on-chain and the maths is the product.
* Verify provably-fair mechanics end to end: the pre-committed server seed hash, client seed changes, nonce incrementing per bet, seed rotation revealing the previous seed, and outcomes a player could independently reproduce from the published algorithm.
* Test each title's own maths: Plinko row counts, risk levels and multiplier grids; Crash cash-out timing, auto-cash-out and multi-bet; Dice roll-over/under targets against payout multiplier and house edge; Roulette inside, outside and neighbour bets against the payout table.
* Validate token precision and rounding per currency decimal places, rounding direction, dust amounts, and the difference between the stored value and the displayed one.
* Reconcile the ledger: deposits, bets, wins and withdrawals against both the platform wallet and the chain, including pending, confirmed and late confirming transactions.
* Hammer concurrency: double-submitted bets, spam betting, the same account open in two tabs or on two devices, and races between a bet and a balance update.
* Probe the limits: minimum and maximum stake per currency, max-win and max-profit caps, and behaviour when a win would exceed the cap.
* Test the failure paths that cost money connection dropped at bet submit, bet placed but the response lost, cash-out fired at the instant of a crash and confirm the balance reconciles afterwards.
* Verify the bet history and the fairness-verification page tell the same story as the API and the chain.
### **Live casino testing**
* Test streamed dealer tables end to end, from lobby listing through to a settled round and the transaction that follows it.
* Pin down bet-window timing: when the window opens and closes against the server clock, whether a last-instant bet is accepted or rejected cleanly, and what happens to a bet that lands after the cut-off.
* Verify game state stays in sync with the studio: dealer action versus client state, the displayed result versus the provider's round result, and a round ID you can trace from the table to the wallet.
* Cover the table games properly blackjack split, double, insurance and bet-behind; roulette inside, outside, neighbour and racetrack bets; side bets such as perfect pairs and 21+3 each checked against its own payout rules.
* Test chips and controls: denominations per currency, rebet, double, undo, table minimums and maximums, and multi-seat or multi-table play.
* Break the real-time layer deliberately: socket dropped mid-round, reconnect, mobile backgrounding, airplane mode, throttled bandwidth, and a frozen stream while the round continues underneath then confirm the balance and outcome are still correct.
* Check the stream itself: latency against game state, quality tiers and auto-degradation, audio, fullscreen, orientation change and picture-in-picture, on real devices and in in-app wallet browsers.
* Validate third-party provider integrations: lobby listings and live stats, launch token and session handling, currency and limit mapping, error codes, and returning to the lobby cleanly.
* Confirm balance sync between our wallet and the provider session, including funds held in a pending round and what happens if the session expires while a bet is live.
* Verify round history and video replay match the settled result, and that responsible-gaming limits and jurisdictional blocks apply correctly mid-session, not just at launch.
### **Across all three**
* Own test strategy for the titles you're responsible for and be accountable for the release call.
* Run functional, regression and exploratory testing across desktop, mobile and tablet, on real devices as well as standard browsers.
* Check the things regulators and players both care about: responsible gaming controls, bet limits, jurisdictional restrictions and correct behaviour across currencies and locales.
* Write and maintain automated tests in our Playwright/TypeScript suite page objects, settlement specs and regression coverage for each new title and raise the bar on how we approach automation as a team.
* Drive our AI-assisted and agent-led testing: use AI agents to accelerate test authoring, extend exploratory coverage, maintain suites against UI churn and triage failures then turn what works into a repeatable practice the rest of the team can use.
* Judge where AI helps and where it doesn't. Agent-generated coverage still has to be reviewed, and a confident wrong answer about a payout is worse than no answer.
* Support UAT and monitor titles after release verify fixes in production, and help triage live incidents when something behaves unexpectedly with real money on the table.
* Raise clear, reproducible bugs in Jira and drive them to resolution with product owners and developers.
* Investigate mobile stability issues crashes, memory pressure, rendering failures and get to a root cause rather than a workaround.
* Spot patterns across the portfolio. A defect that appears in four games usually isn't four bugs.
* Mentor and set standards. As the QA function grows, how we test is partly your design.
* Communicate release readiness honestly: what's tested, what's risky, what isn't ready.
## **What we're looking for**
### **Essential**
* 5+ years in QA on web or mobile products, with real ownership of test strategy rather than just execution.
* Hands-on experience testing at least one of our three core areas slots, crypto/originals games, or live casino and the appetite to own all three.
* Comfortable testing real-time, event-driven products: websocket traffic, state sync, timing windows and recovery after a dropped connection.
* Strong hands-on automation with Playwright, Cypress or Selenium, and genuine comfort in TypeScript or JavaScript. You don't need to be a developer, but you should be able to design, maintain and refactor a suite yourself and explain your choices this is the area where we want you to make us better.
* Real enthusiasm for AI-assisted testing, and hands-on use of AI tooling in your own workflow writing specs, generating test data, triaging failures, reviewing coverage. We want someone who has already started, not someone who intends to.
* An appetite for learning that shows in your history. This space is moving faster than any of us can keep up with; we want the person who reads the changelog, tries the new thing on a real problem, and tells the team what actually worked.
* The instinct to verify against the source of truth. If the balance on screen says one thing and the API response says another, you already know which one you trust.
* An understanding of why floating-point arithmetic and money don't mix.
* Strong exploratory testing the ability to break something that passed every scripted test.
* Experience testing across multiple browsers, devices and screen sizes.
* Confident with Jira and TestRail (or equivalents), and able to write a bug report a developer can act on without a follow-up conversation.
* Able to work independently in a small team, comfortable saying when something isn't ready to ship, and able to hold that line with a product owner.
### **What will set you apart**
* Experience running AI agents as part of testing agents that assist you, or agents you've handed a meaningful part of the job to. Agent-driven exploratory runs, self-maintaining or self-healing suites, LLM-generated specs reviewed into the repo, MCP-connected tooling, agentic failure triage. Tell us what you built, what it caught, and where it let you down.
* A point of view on the limits: how you validate agent output, how you stop a suite from rotting, what you'd never let an agent decide on its own.
* Live casino or live dealer experience, and integration testing against third-party game providers (Evolution, Pragmatic Play Live, Ezugi or similar) lobby, launch, limits, history and replay.
* Video streaming QA: latency, degradation, reconnection behaviour.
* Experience with real-money, payments, sportsbook, trading or other settlement-critical systems.
* Crypto or blockchain exposure wallets, on-chain transactions, token precision.
* Familiarity with provably-fair mechanics (server/client seeds, nonces, hash verification).
* Casino domain knowledge: RTP, paytables, volatility, bonus mechanics, responsible gaming controls.
* Social casino or sweepstakes-model experience.
* Cloud device testing (BrowserStack or similar).
* CI/CD experience getting a suite to run reliably on every build rather than on demand.
* ISTQB / ISEB Foundation or equivalent.

## Job Description
**Join Our Dynamic Team as a Head of Content!** 🌟
Are you passionate about telecoms? Do you thrive in a fast-paced, innovative environment? At Babble, we’re on a mission to be our customer’s most trusted advisor for cloud-based technologies. We’re looking for passionate and talented individuals to join our dynamic team. If so, we have the perfect opportunity for you!
**What will you be doing?**
Own and personally run Babble's content operating system - the core knowledge behind everything we publish, the AI-powered tools built on it, and everything that depends on them being right.
Our content is built on the They Ask, You Answer approach - sometimes called the Endless Customer method: answering the real, specific questions our customers and prospects are actually asking, clearly and honestly, rather than producing generic marketing copy. Done well, this is what earns Babble its reputation as a trusted adviser to the small and medium-sized businesses we work with, not just another technology vendor.
Content is produced through this operating system with the help of AI, but editorial judgement is what makes it good - and it matters most at the two ends of the process: shaping the brief and the standards the AI tools work from at the start, and personally checking, correcting, and approving what comes out at the end. We call this being the human in the loop, and it's the core of the role, not an occasional check.
There is currently one other person in the content function. This role works alongside them day to day and is the final quality check on everything that goes out under Babble's name.
**Accountabilities and Deliverables:**
* Own our core body of knowledge - clear, honest answers to the real questions our customers and prospects ask about cost, problems, comparisons, and what good looks like - and keep it accurate and current.
* Decide where to go deep and where to go light - prioritising the products and topics that matter most to our customers, rather than treating everything as equally important.
* Direct our AI-powered content tools day to day - shaping the brief and standards they work from at the start, and personally checking and correcting what they produce before anything is published.
* Make sure everything we publish is properly organised and easy to find - both for people searching our site and for AI tools like ChatGPT or Google's AI answers.
* Make sure every campaign and every piece of content, whoever produces it, draws on the same accurate, approved information - so Babble never says two different things about the same product.
* Reference pricing and product facts from Babble's single source of truth, rather than restating them independently in content.
* Work day to day alongside the one other person currently in the content function, setting the standard both work to, while remaining personally hands-on rather than only directing.
* Report on content performance in plain terms the CMO can act on.
**Core Competencies:**
* Skilled at turning technical or scattered knowledge into a clear answer a customer would genuinely want to read.
* Editorial judgement - able to prioritise, and to explain and defend that judgement to stakeholders.
* Comfortable being the human in the loop - giving clear direction up front and catching what AI gets wrong at the end, every time, without exception.
* Practical, organised thinker who can define and stick to a simple, consistent structure.
* Comfortable being the person who sends something back if it doesn't meet the standard, regardless of who wrote it.
* Discipline and attention to detail.
* Owner-operator mindset - does the work personally as well as setting the bar for others' output.
* Comfortable with data - reads it and adjusts the plan, not just reports the numbers.
**Key Performance Indicators**
* How fully and clearly we answer the real questions our customers and prospects ask.
* Whether Babble's content is being found and cited by AI search tools (like ChatGPT or Google's AI answers) when people look for answers.
* Growth in people choosing to follow Babble's content directly, rather than us having to chase attention.
* How often our own sales and account teams choose to share the content with customers themselves - a real test of whether it's trusted, not just produced.
## Qualifications
* Strong content or editorial background in a B2B environment - proven ability to define what a business says, not just write it well.
* Familiarity with the They Ask, You Answer (Endless Customer) approach to content is a strong advantage.
* Excellent, precise written English is essential - this role produces content that represents Babble publicly, and the standard of written English will be closely assessed.
* Experience using AI tools in a disciplined, consistent way to produce genuinely high-quality, on-brand content - not generic, unchecked AI output. Experience with agentic AI specifically is a bonus, not a requirement, given how new that technology still is.
* Comfortable working alongside one other person day to day, setting a shared standard rather than working in isolation.
* Experience maintaining consistency and quality across content produced by multiple contributors.
* Confident holding a quality standard and pushing back on stakeholders, including senior ones, when content doesn't meet the bar.

This role is critical because vulnerability management sits at the intersection of several key processes in the CISO operating model. The pre-release security sign-off process checks a service’s open vulnerability backlog before approving a production release — if a service has critical vulnerabilities open beyond SLA, it cannot ship new features. The monthly Risk and Compliance Steerco reviews vulnerability trends as a key risk indicator. The Board receives quarterly reporting on mean time to remediate and open vulnerability counts. The PCI DSS compliance programme depends on quarterly internal and external scanning with clean results. All of this runs through you.
The role requires a particular kind of judgement. You will deal with hundreds or thousands of vulnerability findings from multiple scanning tools (SAST, SCA, DAST, infrastructure scanning, CSPM, container scanning, penetration testing). Most of those findings will not be equally important. Your job is to contextualise them: a critical CVSS vulnerability in an internet-facing payment API is fundamentally different from the same CVSS score on an internal development tool with no access to sensitive data. You prioritise based on exploitability, business context, exposure, and regulatory sensitivity — not just generic severity scores.
If you are someone who combines analytical rigour with excellent stakeholder management skills— someone who can triage a thousand findings into a prioritised, actionable list and then work across a dozen engineering teams to ensure the right things get fixed in the right order — this role will suit you.

Fusion energy offers the potential for significant quantities of low-carbon, inherently safe, abundantly fuelled baseload energy, supporting sustainable climate action and energy independence. While the technical challenge remains high, confidence is increasing, and the rewards of realising fusion are almost incalculable. Anticipated to come online for commercial purposes in the middle of this century, fusion offers a viable means to sustainable net zero in the UK and globally, as well as to increased energy security. The UK is currently a world leader in fusion research and development and in the drive to realise commercially viable energy from fusion, a sector with an estimated value of £tns per year.
STEP (Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production) is the UK’s flagship national programme to deliver a prototype fusion energy plant, targeting 2040, and a path to the commercial viability of fusion. You’ll have the context to see the bigger picture, the freedom to challenge assumptions, and teams that challenge your thinking right back.

* Strong product judgment and a knack for turning messy, ambiguous problems into meaningful outcomes
* Comfort with data: knowing what to measure, what funnels and retention curves are telling you, and when to run an experiment

* Strong technical depth to challenge solutions, make trade-offs, and ship production changes yourself
* A high bar for quality, reliability, performance, security, and customer trust
* A track record of helping others make better decisions and take more ownership
* Clear communication, high ownership, and low ego
* AI fluency: using AI thoughtfully across research, analysis, prototyping, coding, testing, and communication, while staying accountable for quality

* Experience building developer platforms, deployment tools, or products where the developer experience is the product
* You've deployed, configured, and debugged your own workloads on similar platforms
* You’re as comfortable talking to customers as you are digging into the technology
* You naturally think beyond individual features and see how products, systems, and teams fit together

* You bring **10+ years of experience** in commercial product, partnerships product, ad-tech or media product, marketing measurement, or a closely related field, with a track record of shipping products that commercial teams actually sell.

* Attractive compensation package to reward your contributions and growth.
* **40% discount** on all Fever events and experiences + free Candlelight voucher.

# **Build, Scale & Operate Leading DTC Brands alongside A-Players**
## **Maneuver Marketing**
Our Vision, Mission & Success are fuelled by our commitment to be a driving force of positive change to the health of everyday consumers, providing conscious, high-quality & innovative supplement products.

**This is just the beginning of our journey, and you could be part of the next stage of our growth!**
## **Your Next Role**
We are looking for a strategic, commercially minded and highly organized **Senior Manager, Creator Partnerships & Social Commerce** to lead and scale our creator marketing capability.
You will own the end-to-end creator strategy and drive implementation for two women’s health brands. One brand offers supplements that help with symptoms and root causes, and the other offers supplements that support one’s lifestyle habits and addresses nutritional gaps.
Leading a team of two associates who execute the seeding program, you will upgrade and refine our current strategy to build a reliable community of high-quality creator partnerships that strengthen our organic presence, generate commercially valuable content and support our paid media performance.
This is a hands-on management role. You will set the strategy and performance targets, develop the team, improve our systems and processes, and remain directly involved in high-value partnerships and campaign decisions.
The ideal candidate combines strong creator marketing instincts with operational discipline, commercial judgment and a clear understanding of how creator content can be transformed into effective paid advertising.
## **What You’ll Do**
### **1. Own the Creator Strategy Across Both Brands**
* Own creator strategy for two women's health brands across two distinct motions: an established seeding program producing content at volume, and a new TikTok Shop affiliate program built for direct sales.
* Scope is deliberately asymmetric. Seeding covers 4 flagship SKUs today, expanding to all 6 once the team's agentic workflows free the capacity. TikTok Shop launches focused on 2 products under one brand.
* Build creator-driven demand that shows up beyond the platform it originates on: branded search volume, Amazon and Shopify sales lift, and a content library that feeds paid media.
* Identify the right mix of healthcare professionals and content creators for each campaign.
* Establish measurable targets across outreach volume, response rates, partnership approvals, content delivery, cost efficiency and campaign performance.
* Monitor competitor activity, creator pricing and emerging platform trends to keep our approach relevant and competitive.
* Build and deploy AI workflows that increase the team's throughput - creator qualification, outreach personalization at volume, content tagging and rights tracking. We expect measurable capacity gains, not experimentation.
### **2. Lead and Develop the Creator Marketing Team**
* The Meta seeding program is built and running at scale. Your associates own the day-to-day operations; your job is to consult with creative leads, sharpen briefs, run creative tests, and hold quality while the majority of your own attention goes to TikTok and affiliates.
* Oversee the team’s day-to-day outreach, follow-ups, creator communication, fulfilment coordination and administrative workflows.
* Build clear processes and operating rhythms that allow the team to manage a high volume of influencer activity accurately and efficiently.
### **3. Build a Scalable Creator Acquisition Pipeline**
* Source creators across three routes: direct outreach, the TikTok Shop affiliate marketplace, and the established creator network available through our TikTok consultant. Convert the consultant's network into signed, producing partnerships rather than a list.
* Sustain the current output of hundreds of pieces of creator content per month across the seeding program, while building a separate affiliate creator pipeline for TikTok Shop.
* Assess potential partners based on audience fit, content quality, engagement, credibility, pricing and their ability to create or follow relevant trends.
* Develop partnerships with a strong focus on micro- and mid-sized creators, while selectively pursuing larger influencers when commercially justified.
* Create tailored outreach strategies for a competitive market in which larger brands may offer significantly higher creator fees.
### **4. Build the TikTok Shop Affiliate Program**
* Own the TikTok Shop affiliate program for 2 products under one brand, from creator recruitment through commission structure, sample logistics and GMV performance.
* Set and manage commission tiers, open collaborations, targeted invites and any performance-based arrangements; decide where flat-fee and where commission-only makes sense.
* Own affiliate GMV as a number you're accountable for, and the unit economics behind it: cost per acquired affiliate, sample cost per producing creator, blended commission rate.
* Identify and develop the small number of affiliates who will drive the majority of GMV, and build repeat and exclusive arrangements with them.
* Work with the TikTok Affiliate Creative Strategist on creative direction. They own research, concept and brief content; you own creator supply, terms, relationship and program performance.
### **5. Own Campaign Execution and Creator Relationships**
* Oversee partnerships from initial outreach and qualification through contracting, product delivery, content production, payment and performance review.
* Ensure creators receive clear briefs, campaign expectations, timelines and feedback.
* Build strong, professional relationships that encourage creators to become long-term brand advocates rather than one-off partners.
* Maintain an active and engaged creator community through regular updates, challenges, educational content and brand communications.
* Own claims compliance in creator content across both brands. Maintain the do-say/don't-say guidance creators work from, and make sure it holds at volume across seeding, affiliate and organic.
* Ensure FTC material-connection disclosure and platform-specific policy compliance on every partnership. TikTok Shop enforces supplement claims differently from Meta; both need to be handled correctly.
### **6. Turn Creator Content into Growth Assets**
* Secure usage rights and TikTok ad authorization (Spark Ad codes) at the point of partnership, not retroactively.
* Establish a clear process for reviewing, categorizing and distributing creator-generated content.
* Evaluate content based on brand alignment, creative quality, audience relevance and potential commercial use.
* Work with Paid Media, Creative and Marketplace to route creator content to its highest-value use: paid social, marketplace listings, email and brand channels.
* Translate both organic and paid media learnings back into creator briefs so creators can produce stronger, more testable content.
* Supply the brand social channels with a steady flow of approved, on-brand creator content. Publishing and community management on brand-owned accounts sit with a separate role.
### **7. Own Tools, Vendors and Operational Excellence**
* Manage our external partners - the TikTok consultant and content agencies - including scope, output quality, cost and the decision on when capability should move in-house.
* Own the influencer marketing stack end to end. We currently run SARAL; assess whether it, Modash, Lefty or an alternative best serves discovery, outreach, relationship management and reporting at our volume.
* Partner with Supply and Operations teams to ensure product kits are shipped accurately and on time.
* Oversee creator invoicing and payment workflows, ensuring submissions are accurate, approved and processed promptly.
* Identify bottlenecks and introduce scalable workflows, automation and documentation where appropriate.
### **7. Measure and Improve Performance**
* You'll be measured on four things: TikTok Shop affiliate GMV, cost per usable content asset, branded search and marketplace lift attributable to creator activity, and content throughput against quality standard. Everything else is diagnostic.
* You'll manage a defined creator and sampling budget across both programs, with authority to reallocate between seeding and affiliate based on returns.
* Define and monitor the KPIs required to evaluate the health and commercial impact of the influencer program.
* Track outreach volume, open and response rates, approval rates, creator acquisition costs, content delivery, engagement, reach, conversions and return on investment.
* Build clear weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting for the Growth team and company leadership.
* Analyze performance by creator profile, product, platform, partnership structure, outreach message and content format.
* Maintain a structured testing roadmap covering outreach messages, incentives, creator segments and content approaches.
## **How You’ll Succeed**
* You combine strategic thinking with a willingness to remain close to execution.
* You create clarity for your team, hold people accountable and help them improve.
* You build a predictable pipeline of relevant creators and commercially valuable content.
* You use data and experimentation to improve response rates, partnership quality and return on investment.
* You can recognize creators who offer strong value beyond follower count alone.
* You build effective partnerships across Creator Marketing, Paid Media, Creative, Supply, Email Marketing and E-commerce.
* You introduce structure without slowing down execution.
* You communicate clearly, act quickly and resolve problems before they affect campaigns.
* You remain resourceful in a competitive market where budgets and creator expectations may not always align.
* You care equally about relationship quality, operational accuracy and commercial outcomes.
## **What You Bring**
**Required**
* 5+ years in influencer marketing, creator partnerships or creator affiliate marketing, including at least one program you owned end to end with commercial accountability.
* Operator experience running a TikTok Shop or comparable creator affiliate program, with GMV or revenue you were personally accountable for.
* DTC or e-commerce experience in health and wellness, beauty, or another regulated consumer category.
* Experience managing or mentoring team members, with evidence you raised their output rather than just reviewed it.
* Experience managing external agencies, consultants or vendors: setting scope, holding quality, deciding when to bring work in-house.
* Experience structuring and negotiating both flat-fee and performance-based partnerships.
* Strong analytical skills and a track record of using campaign data to change decisions, not just report them.
* Evidence of an AI or automation workflow you built or deployed that measurably increased throughput. Be ready to walk through what it does and what it saved.
**Strongly preferred**
* Ownership of brand-owned organic social channels, not only creator programs. You understand how owned content and creator content compound.
* Working knowledge of FTC material-connection disclosure and platform claim policy in a regulated category. You know what a creator cannot say about a supplement, and why the answer differs on TikTok and Meta.
* Experience collaborating with Paid Media or Creative to repurpose creator content into performance advertising, including securing ad authorization at partnership time.
* Hands-on with an influencer marketing platform - SARAL, Modash, Lefty or equivalent.
* Experience running influencer or creator programs across multiple brands or product categories.
* Experience partnering with healthcare professionals or subject-matter experts as brand partners.
* Understanding of paid social creative testing and direct-response fundamentals.
* Genuine interest in health, wellness, consumer behavior and social media culture.

* A qualification (certificate, diploma or degree) in a life science, IT or related discipline

* The ability to organise and prioritise your own workload with support, rather than direction

We are looking for a Product Manager to join the new Core Payments team at Depop. Core owns the platform, compliance and infrastructure that every payment on Depop depends on: authentication and balance protection, tax and regulatory obligations, the expansion of Depop Payments into new markets, and the reliability and cost of every transaction we process. It is the foundation the rest of our payments products are built on.
This is a role for a Product Manager who is energised by complex, high-stakes platform problems. You'll own a roadmap that spans expanding Depop Payments into new markets meeting marketplace tax and regulatory reporting obligations as Depop scales, protecting user balances through authentication and MFA, and improving the authorisation rate and cost of every transaction we process. Some of this work is non-discretionary - compliance obligations that have to happen regardless of product priorities - and some of it is among the highest-leverage growth work at Depop: operating on Depop Payments drives meaningfully higher checkout conversion, and every market we expand into unlocks new payment methods for buyers and a better payout experience for sellers.

You'll work in a product trio with Design and Engineering, and partner closely with Finance, Legal, Tax, Fraud, Trust & Safety, Payments Operations and CX, as well as external partners such as Stripe. # Senior Transformation Strategist (EU/UK Based - Remote).

## About Duvo
Before Duvo, our founders built and ran a $2 billion retailer. They saw how much critical work still depended on spreadsheets, inboxes, supplier portals and the memory of experienced operators. The real process rarely lived in one system. People held the last mile together.
Duvo is building the Enterprise Execution OS: the shared layer that understands how work really runs, carries it across existing systems and measures the business result.
Our agents do the work, not just suggest the next step. They gather evidence, make decisions within agreed rules, route exceptions to the right person and update the source system. People keep control wherever judgment or approval is needed. Every action leaves an audit trail.
We start with one recurring process and a clear outcome. Every solution carries a contracted 5x ROI guarantee.
## The role
As a Senior Transformation Strategist, you will own the customer's business transformation, not a single Duvo deployment.
You will lead a small portfolio of large enterprise customers. Your job is to set the transformation direction, earn the confidence of senior customer leaders and make the calls that keep the work moving. You are accountable for the business result, the customer relationship and the next wave of value.
You will work alongside Transformation Strategists, who own the day-to-day account presence and workstream execution, and Forward Deployed Engineers, who own the technical solution. Your role is to give both teams a sharp steer, raise the quality of the work and intervene when a decision, relationship or commercial outcome needs senior judgment.
This role needs two kinds of experience that rarely come together: the problem-solving discipline of a strong MBB consultant and the judgment of an operator who has had to live with the result.
## What you will own
### 1. Set the transformation thesis
Start with a view, not a blank page. Learn how the work actually happens, including the exceptions and handoffs that never reach a system of record. Test where the loss sits and focus the customer on the few changes that can take out cost, release cash, protect service, shorten cycle time or strengthen control.
Turn that diagnosis into a clear roadmap: what starts now, what waits, what should not be done, who owns each decision and what evidence could change the plan. Set the few questions and decisions that matter, then direct the team to build the fact base and customer materials needed to answer them.
### 2. Lead the account, not every task
Agree which steps should disappear, which decisions an agent can make, which controls must remain and where people need to stay involved. Establish the account cadence: the right senior forums, clear workstream ownership, decisions, risks and escalation routes. Coach the Transformation Strategist who is present in the account day to day; do not become their substitute.
The technical deployment is only part of the job. You will build the sponsor coalition, handle resistance, fix gaps in ownership and capacity, redesign roles and close the old path. You will review the work closely enough to maintain quality and unblock it, while giving the delivery team room to own it.
### 3. Prove the result and open the next wave
Lock the baseline, target and measurement window before implementation. Track misses as well as successes. Put the result into language a CFO would trust, then get the customer to sign it off.
Once the value is proven, shape the next phase. You own the evidence, strategic case and customer readiness; the commercial owner leads pricing and contracting. Identify expansion opportunities early and convert credible delivery into a larger mandate without compromising the current work.
Your unit of ownership is a business result the customer can sustain. It is not a deck, a deployment, a steering committee or a positive user survey.
## Who we are looking for
You should have both MBB training and real operating experience. We will assess five things:
* **Structured problem solving.** You worked in a core, client-facing role at McKinsey, BCG or Bain. You can take an unfamiliar operation apart, find the critical question and give an executive a clear answer without hiding behind a framework.
* **Operating ownership.** You have built, launched, fixed or grown something inside a company, business unit or startup. The result depended on you after the recommendation was made. Strong evidence includes owning a P&L or revenue target, building a new function or taking a product or operating process from zero to real use.
* **Transformation delivery.** You have personally carried a change from business case through implementation and adoption to a measured outcome. You can explain the baseline, the financial logic, who resisted, what you changed and whether it still worked six months later.
* **Executive and commercial judgment.** You can hold your own with a COO, CFO or board. You know when to challenge, escalate, narrow the scope or stop. You have helped turn a successful first engagement into a larger mandate without losing the trust of the customer.
* **Early-stage working style.** You move without perfect instructions, write clearly and surface bad news early. You use AI seriously in your own work and can reason about the split between agents, people, controls and exceptions. You are choosing Duvo for the work, stage and ownership, not for an AI title.
Experience in retail, CPG, supply chain, logistics, inventory or finance operations will help you ramp faster. It is useful, but it does not replace the five capabilities above.
## What good looks like after 12 months
* You independently own a small set of strategic accounts and can state the financial thesis, stakeholder map, workstream health and next decision for each without opening a deck.
* Each account has a Transformation Strategist with clear day-to-day ownership, a useful senior cadence and fast escalation when judgment is needed.
* Customers can point to verified movement in cost, cash, service, cycle time or control. The old process is closed, or has a committed closure date.
* Proven results have led to credible expansion across functions, business units or markets.
* Your work has improved Duvo's playbook. The next Strategist can reuse your diagnostics, proof methods and adoption mechanisms.
## This role is not for you if
* Your best work ended with the recommendation or target operating model.
* You need a mature playbook, a large support team or stable priorities to perform well.
* You describe impact through workshops, launches, training attendance, estimated hours or stakeholder sentiment rather than business results.
* You want to be the sole hero on every workstream, or cannot delegate meaningful execution while retaining accountability.
* You avoid commercial conversations, direct feedback or visible accountability.
## How we work
* **Own it.** The bar is not “I flagged it.” It is “I moved it forward.” An 80% fix today often beats a perfect answer next week.
* **Stay close to the customer.** Know their real day better than the process document. If they ask us to automate something broken, show them a better way.
* **Prove it and say it straight.** Measure before you propose. Share bad news when you have it. Strong opinions are welcome; defending them after the evidence changes is not.
* **Use AI and work in public.** We use AI on our own work and remain responsible for the output. We write things down in English so someone who missed the meeting can still follow.
* **Bring intensity and judgment.** A good answer can still lose if it arrives too late. The pace is high because the team is small and the customer work is live. Commitment comes from the work, not monitoring or guilt.
## Location and travel
This role is remote across the UK and Europe. Expect regular travel and working on site with customers for multiple days in a week when projects are live.
## What we offer
* Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, with flexibility in the balance between cash and ownership.
* Direct access to founders, customers and decisions.
* The budget and autonomy to use the best AI tools available.
* A product already producing measured results in live enterprise operations.
* The chance to help define how Duvo, and its customers, approach AI-led transformation.
## How we hire
1. **Competency interview.** A detailed look at transformations you personally led and the results you produced.
2. **Live case.** An enterprise problem that tests structure, numbers, prioritisation and executive communication.
3. **Founder conversation.** A candid discussion about the role, Duvo and whether this is the environment for you.
We move quickly and give direct feedback throughout.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale - unleashing the potential of businesses and people. We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to join Platform Infrastructure - Application Networking and set where Elastic Cloud application networking goes next. This work covers Ingress, security controls, private connectivity, and DNS management - the path every interaction with Elasticsearch, Kibana, and the broader Elastic stack takes. You will drive the technical vision, architecture, and design of these systems, not just execute against an existing roadmap.
This is a Principal-level role for an engineer who has designed high-performance, scalable networking platforms and can drive technical initiatives across organizations. Elastic is investing in the reliability, security, and reach of Elastic Cloud; you will hold a high bar for those qualities while other engineering teams rely on what this platform provides.

* Set the technical direction for major application networking initiatives, owning designs from proposal through general availability.
* Lead the development of Ingress, private connectivity, DNS, and security controls on a large scale for Elastic Cloud. Continuously identify and address issues related to performance, reliability, and operability.
* Lead multi-quarter, cross-organizational projects that other Elastic engineering teams rely on, and guide these projects through to delivery.
* Raise the operational quality of our services. Take charge of operational investigations from beginning to end. Lead complex incident investigations and reviews. Participate in on-call rotation.

* Partner with and advise product management and senior engineering stakeholders on technical trade-offs, feasibility, and roadmap direction.
* Identify and champion improvements to security, stability, and cost efficiency before they become problems. Untangle complexity and bring architectural clarity across the platform.
### What You Bring:
* Experience with building software, including setting technical direction for complex distributed systems running production at scale (Staff or Principal level, or equivalent scope).
* Deep expertise in application networking and cloud-native architecture. You should understand how services communicate at scale. Knowledge of how to design, operate, and evolve Ingress, private connectivity, DNS, and security controls is required.
* You have experience building large-scale distributed systems, rather than making use of off-the-shelf services.

* You can work autonomously, drive decisions and results in a distributed team by leveraging asynchronous, direct, and transparent communication. You communicate clearly and can influence direction across teams and levels without formal authority.
### Bonus Points:
* Hands-on experience with Kubernetes networking (Cilium, external-dns, Envoy Gateway, and Crossplane) and with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and its networking ecosystem.

As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. We're looking for a developer to grow Ember's network of charging hubs. You'll find the sites, take them through legals and planning, manage the build and energise them. How you work and think matters more to us than which industry you've worked in. You think clearly, can run several projects at once and are as at home on a site as behind a desk.
About Ember
We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.
Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation — everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.
We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and ~100 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level.
The role
Charging hubs are Ember's key growth enabler. They give us the ultra-fast charge points we need to run our network, and they act as a base for our fleet — parking, washing, driver lounges and more. We have hubs across Scotland today, with additional sites across the UK under construction or in the pipeline.
You'll join a small team of four, taking end-to-end responsibility for your own sites and helping out on others. We're typically running a handful of projects at any one time.
Step one is finding a site. You’ll need to think about where we need charging capacity to support future routes, scout industrial estates and brownfield plots and reach out to commercial agents, local authorities and landlords. Some great sites are advertised but many are not, so landing one usually means being patient and creative.
Once you've got a site, we move on to lease negotiations, design, the planning application and the power connection. You'll work with network operators to land the grid connection, and with our suppliers to procure, install and commission the charging equipment. Solicitors, architects and engineers are there to help, but the project is yours to drive — you set the direction, you ask the difficult questions and you make the trade-offs.
It’s important to be hands-on. We don't go to tender and leave the rest to an outsourced project manager — we want you on site, asking why a kerb is in the wrong place. Even after a site is live, our involvement doesn't stop. The team keeps refining and improving every site, and you'll be part of that work across the network, not just on the sites you've built yourself.
Diversity and equality
At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.
Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.
What's on offer
You'll receive a salary of £55,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home, with an expectation that you'll spend some time travelling to different sites.
How do I apply?
Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you.
Applications close Friday 2 October at 5pm.
Who we're looking for
You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you:
Curious and quick to learn. You're comfortable in unfamiliar territory — new technical specs, new legal terms, new planning processes — and you treat each one as an opportunity to learn. You don't expect to know everything on day one.
Engineering mindset. You're the sort of person who'll happily watch YouTube videos explaining concrete reinforcement, three-phase distribution or substation transformers. You'll be excited to dive into the same level of detail on our projects.
A first-principles thinker. You take problems back to fundamentals rather than reaching for jargon or the way things are usually done. When you work with experts — solicitors, architects, engineers — you treat them as people you can learn from, not people you can outsource your thinking to.
Commercially astute. You can tell when something is worth fighting for and when it's better to redesign around a constraint, whether that's a lease, a planning condition or a contractor's quote.
Highly organised. Managing a pipeline of projects is complex, with many timelines, people to chase, details to look into and things that can (and will) go wrong. We want you at Inbox Zero, not in inbox hell.
Comfortable using AI. At a minimum you use it as part of how you work — to learn faster, draft documents and get to the bottom of unfamiliar topics. But maybe you’ll go further and build software to help the team work faster and more precisely.
Hands-on. Hubs are built in the real world, not behind a screen. You'll meet landlords, talk to electricians and look at drains, but you'll also need to read contracts and chase agents who've gone quiet.
A strong sense of what good looks like. Whatever the topic, problem or issue. You need to know how to hold yourself and others to a high standard.

The Entain vision is to be the world leader in sports betting and gaming entertainment by creating the most exciting and trusted experience for our customers.
As the **Third-Party Risk Management Senior Manager,** you will support the implementation and ongoing operation of Entain's Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) platform and framework, working closely with risk subject matter experts, Procurement, business owners, and other key stakeholders to ensure proportionate third-party risk processes are embedded and sustained across the organisation.

This is a hands-on role and will be important in embedding effective Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) practices, supporting the development of a consistent risk methodology, configuring TPRM processes and workflows, and running high-quality BAU activity across the Entain group.
**Key Responsibilities:**
* **TPRM framework support:** Coordinate and support the ongoing development and operation of a Procurement-led, group-wide third-party risk management framework, working with risk SMEs and business stakeholders to ensure end-to-end TPRM processes are implemented, maintained, and aligned with regulatory expectations, industry good practice, and business needs.
